maximum_pilot.reason: Current evidence supports offline, replay, report-only and shadow experiments only; no independently validated production improvement was established today.

findings.observed: A 24 Aug 2026 football benchmark used 225,474 matches from 2018-2026 with a strictly chronological split; recent-form/Elo state must be constructed from information available before each fixture. This reinforces leakage-safe evaluation as a first-class requirement.
findings.derived: ARGUS should treat point-in-time reconstructability at decision_time as a research invariant for features, calibration, market snapshots and live state.
findings.hypothesis: A report-only audit may expose optimistic historical evaluation caused by fallback statistics, late enrichment or settlement-time leakage.
findings.smallest_safe_experiment: Replay at least 1,000 frozen decisions and verify every feature timestamp <= decision_time; inject known future-data contamination as positive controls.
findings.required_evidence: At least 1,000 decisions across multiple competitions plus synthetic leakage controls.
findings.failure_condition: High false-positive rate or inability to distinguish event_time, ingest_time, decision_time and settlement_time.
findings.rollback: Keep validator report-only and make no inference-path changes.

findings.observed: A May 2026 in-play football study calibrated a continuous-time goal model to Betfair 1X2 and over/under prices at kick-off and found market calibration was the dominant driver of predictive accuracy across 140 EPL matches; post-shot xG supplied additional time-varying live information.
findings.derived: Pre-match market information should remain a strong live prior and should be moved only by temporally valid in-play evidence rather than repeatedly rebuilt from scratch.
findings.hypothesis: A market-anchored live challenger may improve calibration and stability, especially during sparse-event periods.
findings.smallest_safe_experiment: Historical minute-level replay comparing current live probabilities with a market-anchored challenger; paper/shadow only.
findings.required_evidence: At least 500 matches and 5,000 live snapshots, with score/card/state-change strata and chronological evaluation.
findings.failure_condition: No repeatable Brier/log-loss/risk-coverage gain or gains dependent on future/closing information.
findings.rollback: Delete challenger; retain current live champion.

findings.observed: scikit-learn 1.9 documentation states calibration data should be independent from model-fitting data; isotonic calibration is more prone to overfitting on small samples and is generally favored only with enough data (roughly >1,000 samples). Temperature scaling is a low-parameter multiclass calibration option.
findings.derived: ARGUS calibration should be chronological, disjoint from training and sample-gated; UNAVAILABLE is preferable to forcing a calibrator on sparse segments.
findings.hypothesis: Temperature or sigmoid scaling may be more stable than isotonic for sparse league/market segments.
findings.smallest_safe_experiment: Offline rolling-origin comparison of RAW vs sigmoid vs temperature; permit isotonic only above a declared minimum sample gate.
findings.required_evidence: At least three forward folds; report Brier, log-loss, reliability curves and sample counts per probability region.
findings.failure_condition: Improvement is confined to calibration folds, worsens the next chronological fold, or creates unstable extreme probabilities.
findings.rollback: Keep RAW or previous champion calibrator.

findings.observed: June 2026 selective time-series forecasting research models expected forecast difficulty and reports that rejecting predicted-hard cases improves accuracy across coverage levels; February 2026 multi-horizon abstention research shows horizon structure matters. Neither result is football-specific.
findings.derived: ARGUS should test abstention as a risk-versus-coverage decision, potentially conditioned on horizon, freshness, disagreement and state volatility rather than confidence alone.
findings.hypothesis: A difficulty-aware rejection layer may reduce selective error without collapsing actionable coverage.
findings.smallest_safe_experiment: Paper-only meta-model predicting next-fold error percentile; compare risk-coverage curves against current abstention logic.
findings.required_evidence: At least 5,000 settled predictions clustered by match and at least three chronological folds; separate prematch and live.
findings.failure_condition: Threshold instability, poor league transfer, or unacceptable coverage collapse.
findings.rollback: Discard challenger and keep current abstention policy.

findings.observed: Current Redis cache-aside guidance treats TTL as an explicit bound on staleness, recommends invalidation on source changes and supports stampede mitigation for repeated concurrent reads.
findings.derived: ARGUS API savings should be state-aware: long TTL for static metadata, tighter TTL for prematch, and very short/event-invalidated caching for decision-critical live state.
findings.hypothesis: State-aware TTL plus request coalescing can reduce duplicate provider calls without increasing stale actionable decisions.
findings.smallest_safe_experiment: Shadow cache simulation only: continue authoritative reads while computing which calls would be avoided and whether cached data would miss score/card/status transitions.
findings.required_evidence: At least 7 match-days and 10,000 candidate reads including material live transitions.
findings.failure_condition: Any policy class repeatedly serves stale decision-critical state or cost savings are negligible.
findings.rollback: Do not activate cache behavior; retain measurements only.

findings.observed: Prometheus guidance recommends urgent, important, actionable, real alerts and symptom-based paging; OpenTelemetry semantic conventions standardize naming across traces, metrics and logs.
findings.derived: ARGUS should distinguish operator-impacting symptoms (stale actionable state, settlement blocked, ledger unavailable) from technical causes, while making each decision traceable end-to-end.
findings.hypothesis: A normalized decision envelope can reduce false alarms and shorten failure diagnosis without touching forecasting logic.
findings.smallest_safe_experiment: Emit shadow telemetry for decision_id, match_id, phase, provider, event_time, ingest_time, decision_time, freshness_ms, model_version, data_quality_state, settlement_state and error_type.
findings.required_evidence: At least 14 days of parallel telemetry and review of all real incidents in that window.
findings.failure_condition: Excessive cardinality, loss of provenance, or a genuine operator-impacting incident is obscured.
findings.rollback: Disable shadow emitter; preserve current alerts.

findings.observed: Current MLflow Model Registry documentation formalizes immutable model versions, lineage, aliases such as champion and validation-status tags, enabling reversible promotion workflows.
findings.derived: ARGUS can adopt the governance semantics without necessarily adding MLflow: champion_version, challenger_version, evaluation_window, promotion_gate and rollback_target should be explicit machine-readable state.
findings.hypothesis: Minimal native registry semantics may improve Maximum Pilot safety and reproducibility at near-zero runtime cost.
findings.smallest_safe_experiment: Add a non-runtime research schema for champion/challenger metadata and validate it on historical promotions only.
findings.required_evidence: Successful reconstruction of at least three historical model/config changes with complete lineage and rollback target.
findings.failure_condition: Schema cannot identify exact code/data/config lineage or creates a second conflicting source of truth.
findings.rollback: Remove the experimental registry artifact; do not install new infrastructure.

findings.observed: Recent football benchmarking with a large chronological dataset shows that multiple model families can perform similarly and that market-informed baselines remain difficult to beat; a 2026 Bundesliga study likewise emphasizes calibration and distinct information rather than architecture novelty.
findings.derived: Model complexity should not be promoted unless it adds stable out-of-sample information beyond existing market and football features.
findings.hypothesis: None promoted; novelty alone is not an ARGUS objective.
findings.smallest_safe_experiment: None required unless a concrete challenger has new information and a pre-registered evaluation plan.
findings.required_evidence: Repeatable chronological proper-score improvement plus calibration stability and useful selective coverage.

explicit_non_actions: No staking or bankroll logic changed.
No research result is represented as deployed.
